name: The Bargain and the Blade
setup: The Abyssal offers you terms before the first exchange, and will offer again after each one. Every offer is genuine and fairly priced. That is what makes it a duel and not a mugging.

opponent.name: an Abyssal of the Descent
opponent._poolsDerived_20260905: health removed: it was on the retired 3-7 scale and overrode a live synthesised sheet, which made a bout end in a median of ONE turn. The pool now derives from standing (30 + 5/level) through the level the threat implies. `yieldAtFraction` replaces an absolute `yieldAt` because a ratio is scale-free.

party.ifYouBringPeople: ⛔ THE ABYSSAL PRICES A PARTY DIFFERENTLY, AND SAYS SO. Terms offered to three people are cheaper per head and more expensive in total — ⚠️ and it will offer one of you a price the others do not hear. ⚑ Every offer stays genuine and fairly priced; that is what makes it dangerous.
party.whatItAsksOfAParty: ⛔ Whether you decide together. ⚠️ It never lies about the cost, so a party that loses here chose to.
party.foldNote: ⚑ A folded INFLUENCE ally can price the offer back. ⛔ Nobody can refuse it FOR you.

_partyClauseWhy: ⛔ THE PARTY CLAUSE — R36/R36a, authored 2026-09-05. Every encounter in the corpus was written when a fight was ONE PERSON AGAINST ONE OPPONENT. ⚑ R36 makes a party member fight from their own sheet; R36a caps three acting fully and folds the rest. ⚠️ THE CLAUSE IS ADDITIVE — no prose changed. It is what a GM reads when more than one person is present.
